title: The 6 Best Smart TVs of 2026 - RTINGS.com
content:
# The 6 Best Smart TVs of 2026
All new 4k TVs have a smart platform that includes features and apps. Some manufacturers use proprietary platforms, such as Samsung with its [Tizen OS](/tv/learn/what-is-tizen) and LG with its [webOS](/tv/learn/what-is-webos), while others prefer to integrate third-party options like [Google TV](/tv/learn/what-is-google-tv) or Roku. Most TVs offer a very similar selection of smart features, so you shouldn't really choose a TV based solely on its smart features. Most TVs have all of the common apps, but you should check your service provider for local channels that might not be available on all platforms if you care about that. You can always add an external player like an Apple TV 4K if you're looking for something a bit more versatile, or if you've found that perfect TV but it lacks the one app you really need.

Below are our recommendations for the best smart televisions. This article takes a very broad approach, but if you're looking for something a little more specific, check out our picks for the [best TVs for watching movies](/tv/reviews/best/by-usage/movies), the [best TVs for watching sports](/tv/reviews/best/by-usage/sports), or the [best gaming TVs](/tv/reviews/best/by-usage/video-gaming). You can also [vote](/review-pipeline/tv) on which TVs you want us to buy and test. To learn more about the 2026 TV landscape, check out our [2026 TV lineup page](/tv/learn/2026-lineup).

## Best Smart TV
The Samsung S95H OLED is the best smart TV we've tested. This TV delivers exceptionally good picture quality, with deep, inky blacks in a dark room and vibrant colors. While OLED TVs like this one are typically known for their dark-room performance, the S95H is one of the first truly versatile OLED TVs that's nearly as good in a bright room. Its matte anti-reflective coating and high peak brightness make glare a thing of the past. There's a downside to this, though, as blacks aren't as deep, and the screen has a purple tint when viewed during the day.

It also comes loaded with a wide selection of gaming features like a high refresh rate and HDMI 2.1 bandwidth on all four inputs, so you can take full advantage of the latest gaming consoles or a recent gaming PC. It's a feature-packed smart TV, running Samsung's proprietary Tizen OS smart interface. This easy-to-use platform has a huge selection of streaming apps, including many game streaming services that let you play the latest games directly on the TV. Samsung also promises up to seven years of platform updates for it, so you'll continue to receive system updates that may even add new features down the line.

## Best Upper Mid-Range Smart TV
If you want something a bit cheaper, you can step down to the LG C6 OLED 2026 instead. This incredible TV delivers nearly identical dark room performance to the Samsung S95H OLED above, with deep, inky blacks that give the TV an almost 3D look. It's not as bright, though, and it has a glossy coating, so glare is a bit more distracting during the day, and bright scenes aren't quite as impactful. The exact performance varies depending on which size you're looking at, though. The 77- and 83-inch models are sold as the LG C6H OLED instead, and they, along with the 48-inch C6, are much more colorful than the other sizes and perform much closer to the S95H.

As for smart features, the C6 doesn't disappoint. While it uses a different smart platform than the S95H, known as webOS, it has an equally great selection of streaming apps, so you can quickly find your favorite content. It also supports user profiles, so you can keep your viewing habits separate from your spouse or kids. Finally, it has fantastic support for smart home integrations, including support for the latest Matter devices, so you can easily control your existing smart devices straight from the TV.

## Best Mid-Range Smart TV
The [nolink:LG B6 OLED 2026] is the best mid-range TV we've tested. This entry-level OLED delivers the same fantastic dark room performance as the LG C6 OLED 2026 above, but it's not as bright. This decrease in brightness makes this TV a better choice for someone watching mainly in a dim or moderately lit room, whereas the C6 and even more expensive Samsung S95H OLED are better choices for a bright room.

Like the C6, it's a well-rounded gaming TV with four HDMI 2.1 inputs that let you take full advantage of the latest consoles. It's limited to a 120Hz refresh rate, though, so it's not as versatile for PC gamers. As for smart features, it has the same selection as the C6 above, including LG's Magic Remote, which lets you navigate menus by pointing at them. There's also a cheaper version of this TV, known as the LG B6E OLED. It's the same TV, just with a basic remote instead of the previously mentioned Magic Remote. Depending on local deals, you may be able to find either of these models cheaper.

## Best Lower Mid-Range Smart TV
You can save a lot of money by stepping down to a lower mid-range model like the Hisense U7SG, but there are some noticeable trade-offs. While it looks good in a dark room, blacks are nowhere near as deep as they are on the OLED models above. This means you'll see some haloing around bright objects in a dark room, and the image doesn't pop out the same way. It still delivers a great overall experience, with very high peak brightness and vibrant colors for a more impactful viewing experience, and it has great out-of-the-box accuracy.

As for smart features, this model runs the Google TV smart interface, which supports most of the same features as the proprietary options above. It's a great choice if you have other Google-powered devices, like a smartphone, and many of your content purchases carry over seamlessly. Like the [LG B6 OLED 2026](/tv/reviews/lg/b6-oled-2026) above, it also has great smart home support, so you can quickly integrate it into your existing network and control your other smart devices with minimal setup.

## Best Budget Smart TV
If you're shopping on a budget and don't want to sacrifice much on picture quality, check out the Hisense U6SF Pro instead. While it's not as bright or as colorful as the Hisense U7SG above, it still delivers surprisingly good picture quality, with high peak brightness, vibrant colors, and excellent contrast. It isn't quite as refined as the U7SG, as its local dimming has significantly fewer dimming zones, so you'll see more haloing and transition artifacts around bright details and subtitles.

Another significant difference between these two TVs is their smart features. While the U7SG ships with the Google TV smart interface, the U6SF runs Amazon's [nolink:Fire TV] smart platform instead. It still has a great selection of streaming apps and home integrations, but it's nowhere near as customizable as Google.

## Best Cheap Smart TV
If you just want a feature-rich TV and don't care as much about picture quality, the Vizio Mini LED Quantum 4K is the best cheap smart TV we've tested. Despite its extremely cheap price, it delivers okay picture quality, with incredibly high peak brightness and pretty good colors. The main trade-off between it and the Hisense U6SF Pro above is dark room performance. The Vizio has a local dimming feature, but it's nowhere near as good as the Hisense's, so you'll see a lot more haloing around bright parts of the screen when you're watching TV at night, and blacks just aren't as deep.

As for smart features, it's an alright TV overall. It runs Vizio's proprietary VIZIO OS smart interface. It's a fairly quick, easy-to-use smart platform that looks a lot like Google TV, but it has a more limited selection of apps and is a bit buggy at times. You'll still find all the big players in the streaming industry, but some niche services that are only available in select markets are less likely to be available. You also have to sign in with a Walmart account to use the TV's smart features, but all of the higher-end models have sign-in requirements, too.

## What Is A Smart TV?
A smart TV is a television connected to the internet that provides web-related features. It has built-in apps for streaming and usually an app store where you can download your favorite apps. Built-in smart platforms are similar to streaming boxes from Apple and Roku, and while smart TVs were once much slower, they've gotten a lot better over the past few years.

Not only does almost every TV include smart features, but most of them are also pretty good. Most shoppers will be pleased by the features of any of the smart platforms. Don't fret too much about features if you're shopping for the best TV for streaming, because the picture quality is still more important. Instead, focus on picture quality or other features that complement your usage, and you'll get much closer to finding your perfect TV.

Learn more about [smart platforms](/tv/learn/best-smart-features).

## All Reviews
Our recommendations are based on what we think are the best TVs for streaming currently available with smart features. They are adapted to be valid for most people in each price range, so this article will help you find the best smart TV for the money in your budget. The rating is based on our review, factoring in price and feedback from our visitors.

If you would like to do the work of choosing yourself, here is a list of all our recent reviews of smart TVs. Be careful not to get too caught up in the details. While no TV is perfect, most TVs are great enough to please almost everyone, and the differences are often not noticeable unless you really look for them.
